title: HIVE Doctor — Anatomy Reference (kinesiology-style, all systems)
author: Jeff
safety: Educational anatomy reference for adults. Not a diagnosis. Reproductive sections are clinical/educational. Pending clinician sign-off.

systems.title: Anatomical position, planes & regions
systems.overview: Anatomy is described from the 'anatomical position': standing, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms forward. Directions and planes give everyone a shared map of the body.

structures.name: Directional terms
structures.detail: Superior/inferior (up/down), anterior/posterior (front/back), medial/lateral (toward/away from midline), proximal/distal (near/far from the trunk), superficial/deep.

structures.name: Planes
structures.detail: Sagittal (left/right), coronal/frontal (front/back), transverse/axial (top/bottom).

structures.name: Abdominal regions
structures.detail: Nine regions, or four quadrants (RUQ, LUQ, RLQ, LLQ) used to locate belly pain.

structures.name: Body cavities
structures.detail: Cranial (brain), thoracic (heart/lungs), abdominal, and pelvic cavities.

systems.normal: A shared reference frame; no 'normal/abnormal' — it's the language the rest of anatomy uses.
common_problems: Mislocating pain — e.g., appendicitis pain is classically RLQ; gallbladder RUQ.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Bones & the skeleton
systems.overview: The adult skeleton has 206 bones. It supports the body, protects organs, anchors muscles for movement, stores calcium, and makes blood cells in the marrow.

structures.name: Axial skeleton
structures.detail: Skull, spine (cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacrum, coccyx), ribs (12 pairs), sternum — protects brain, cord, heart, lungs.

structures.name: Appendicular skeleton
structures.detail: Shoulder girdle, arms (humerus, radius, ulna, hand), pelvis, legs (femur, tibia, fibula, foot) — for movement.

structures.name: Bone types
structures.detail: Long (femur), short (wrist), flat (skull, ribs), irregular (vertebrae).

structures.name: Bone structure
structures.detail: Hard outer cortical bone, spongy inner trabecular bone, and marrow (blood-cell factory).

systems.normal: Bones are dense and non-tender, aligned and symmetrical left-to-right; a limb matches its opposite in length and shape.
common_problems: Fractures (breaks), osteoporosis (thinning/fragile bone), osteoarthritis (joint wear), scoliosis (spine curve), bone infection, bone tumours.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Joints, ranges & movements
systems.overview: Joints are where bones meet. Most movement happens at freely-moving (synovial) joints, cushioned by cartilage and lubricated by fluid, held by ligaments and moved by muscles.

structures.name: Joint types
structures.detail: Ball-and-socket (shoulder, hip — move all directions), hinge (elbow, knee — bend/straighten), pivot (neck rotation), gliding (wrist), saddle (thumb).

structures.name: Support tissues
structures.detail: Cartilage (smooth cushion), ligaments (bone-to-bone), tendons (muscle-to-bone), bursae (friction-reducing sacs), joint capsule + synovial fluid.

structures.name: Movements
structures.detail: Flexion/extension (bend/straighten), abduction/adduction (away/toward midline), rotation, circumduction, pronation/supination (palm down/up), inversion/eversion (sole in/out), dorsiflexion/plantarflexion (foot up/down).

systems.normal: Smooth, pain-free movement through a full expected range, equal to the other side, without swelling, heat, locking, or instability.
common_problems: Sprains (ligament), strains (muscle/tendon), dislocations, arthritis (osteo/rheumatoid/gout), bursitis, tendinitis, torn cartilage, frozen shoulder.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Muscles & movement
systems.overview: Over 600 skeletal muscles move the body by contracting and pulling on bones across joints. Muscles work in pairs — one shortens (agonist) while its partner relaxes (antagonist). There are also smooth muscle (organs) and cardiac muscle (heart).

structures.name: How it works
structures.detail: A muscle attaches at an origin (fixed) and insertion (moving) point; contracting shortens it and moves the insertion toward the origin.

structures.name: Major upper-body
structures.detail: Deltoids (shoulder), pectorals (chest), biceps/triceps (arm), trapezius & lats (back), rotator cuff (shoulder stability), abdominals, erector spinae (spine).

structures.name: Major lower-body
structures.detail: Gluteals (hip), quadriceps (knee extend), hamstrings (knee bend), gastrocnemius/soleus (calf), hip flexors, adductors.

structures.name: Muscle types
structures.detail: Skeletal (voluntary), smooth (involuntary — gut, vessels), cardiac (heart).

systems.normal: Muscles are symmetrical, with normal bulk and tone, full strength against resistance, and no wasting, twitching, or fixed weakness.
common_problems: Strains/tears, cramps, tendinitis, muscle wasting, myositis, rhabdomyolysis (breakdown), neuromuscular disease, fibromyalgia (widespread pain).
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Heart & blood vessels
systems.overview: The heart is a four-chambered muscular pump that drives blood through two circuits: to the lungs for oxygen, and to the body to deliver it. It beats about 60–100 times a minute at rest.

structures.name: Chambers
structures.detail: Right atrium & ventricle (pump blood to the lungs), left atrium & ventricle (pump oxygen-rich blood to the body — the left ventricle is the strongest).

structures.name: Valves
structures.detail: Tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic — one-way doors that stop backflow; their closing makes the 'lub-dub'.

structures.name: Vessels
structures.detail: Arteries carry blood away from the heart (high pressure), veins return it, capillaries exchange oxygen/nutrients. The aorta is the main artery; coronary arteries feed the heart itself.

structures.name: Electrical system
structures.detail: The SA node sets the rhythm; signals spread to make the chambers beat in order.

structures.name: Pulse points
structures.detail: Radial (wrist), carotid (neck), brachial (arm), femoral (groin), pedal (foot).

systems.normal: A regular pulse 60–100/min at rest, blood pressure around 120/80, warm well-perfused limbs, no chest pain, breathlessness, or swelling.
common_problems: Heart attack (blocked coronary artery), angina, heart failure, arrhythmias (e.g., atrial fibrillation), valve disease, high blood pressure, aneurysm, DVT/PE, peripheral arterial disease.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Airway & lungs
systems.overview: The respiratory system brings air in, exchanges oxygen for carbon dioxide in the lungs, and breathes the waste out. The diaphragm does most of the work of breathing.

structures.name: Upper airway
structures.detail: Nose/mouth, pharynx (throat), larynx (voice box with the epiglottis that guards the airway).

structures.name: Lower airway
structures.detail: Trachea (windpipe) → two bronchi → smaller bronchioles → alveoli (tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens).

structures.name: Lungs
structures.detail: Right lung (3 lobes), left lung (2 lobes, smaller — the heart sits there), wrapped in pleura.

structures.name: Muscles
structures.detail: Diaphragm (main), intercostals between the ribs; accessory neck muscles when struggling.

systems.normal: Quiet, effortless breathing ~12–20/min at rest, full sentences, no wheeze or noisy breathing, oxygen ≥95%, both sides of the chest moving equally.
common_problems: Asthma, COPD, pneumonia, bronchitis, pulmonary embolism, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), pleurisy, lung cancer, croup (children).
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Gut & digestion
systems.overview: The digestive tract is a ~9-metre tube that breaks food down, absorbs nutrients, and removes waste, helped by the liver, pancreas, and gallbladder.

structures.name: Upper tract
structures.detail: Mouth → oesophagus → stomach (acid + churning) → small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum — most absorption).

structures.name: Lower tract
structures.detail: Large intestine/colon (water absorption) → rectum → anus.

structures.name: Accessory organs
structures.detail: Liver (processes nutrients, makes bile, detoxifies — RUQ), gallbladder (stores bile), pancreas (digestive enzymes + insulin).

structures.name: Appendix
structures.detail: Small pouch at the start of the large intestine (RLQ) — can become inflamed (appendicitis).

systems.normal: Comfortable eating and swallowing, no persistent pain, regular bowel habit, no blood in stool, stable weight, no jaundice.
common_problems: Reflux/GERD, gastritis/ulcers, appendicitis, gallstones, pancreatitis, hepatitis, IBS/IBD, diverticulitis, bowel obstruction, coeliac, GI bleeding, colorectal cancer.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Brain, cord & nerves
systems.overview: The nervous system is the body's control and communication network. The brain and spinal cord (central nervous system) process information; nerves (peripheral) carry signals in and out.

structures.name: Brain regions
structures.detail: Cerebrum (thought, movement, senses — in lobes: frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital), cerebellum (balance/coordination), brainstem (breathing, heart rate, consciousness).

structures.name: Spinal cord
structures.detail: Runs in the spine; relays signals and handles reflexes. Damage affects function below the level.

structures.name: Nerves
structures.detail: 12 cranial nerves (face/head), spinal nerves to the body; sensory (in), motor (out), and autonomic (automatic — heart, gut).

structures.name: Protection
structures.detail: Skull, vertebrae, meninges (membranes), and cerebrospinal fluid.

systems.normal: Clear thinking, normal speech, equal strength and sensation on both sides, steady balance, equal reactive pupils, normal coordination.
common_problems: Stroke/TIA, seizures, migraine, meningitis, concussion/head injury, Parkinson's, dementia, MS, neuropathy, Bell's palsy, Guillain-Barré, brain tumour.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Glands & hormones
systems.overview: The endocrine system is a set of glands that release hormones into the blood to control slow, body-wide processes — metabolism, growth, stress, reproduction, and blood sugar.

structures.name: Pituitary
structures.detail: 'Master gland' at the brain's base — directs other glands.

structures.name: Thyroid
structures.detail: Neck gland setting metabolic rate (energy, temperature, weight).

structures.name: Adrenals
structures.detail: Atop the kidneys — stress hormones (cortisol, adrenaline), salt/water balance.

structures.name: Pancreas (islets)
structures.detail: Insulin and glucagon — control blood sugar.

structures.name: Gonads
structures.detail: Ovaries/testes — sex hormones.

structures.name: Parathyroids
structures.detail: Calcium balance.

systems.normal: Stable energy, weight, temperature tolerance, mood, and blood sugar; normal growth and periods.
common_problems: Diabetes, hypo/hyperthyroidism, adrenal insufficiency (Addison's)/excess (Cushing's), PCOS, pituitary disorders.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Kidneys & bladder
systems.overview: The urinary system filters the blood, removes waste and extra water as urine, and balances salts, fluid, and blood pressure.

structures.name: Kidneys
structures.detail: Two bean-shaped organs (flank/back) filtering blood into urine and controlling fluid, salts, and blood pressure.

structures.name: Ureters
structures.detail: Tubes carrying urine from each kidney to the bladder.

structures.name: Bladder
structures.detail: Muscular storage sac that signals when full.

structures.name: Urethra
structures.detail: Tube that carries urine out (longer in males, passing the prostate).

systems.normal: Passing urine comfortably several times a day, pale-yellow, no blood, no burning, good control, no flank pain.
common_problems: UTI, kidney infection, kidney stones, chronic kidney disease, incontinence, retention, bladder/kidney cancer, enlarged prostate (affects flow).
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Skin, hair & nails
systems.overview: The skin is the body's largest organ — a waterproof barrier that protects, senses touch, controls temperature, and makes vitamin D.

structures.name: Epidermis
structures.detail: Thin outer layer — barrier and pigment (melanin).

structures.name: Dermis
structures.detail: Deeper layer with nerves, blood vessels, sweat and oil glands, hair roots, collagen.

structures.name: Subcutaneous fat
structures.detail: Insulation and cushioning beneath.

structures.name: Appendages
structures.detail: Hair, nails, sweat glands, sebaceous (oil) glands.

systems.normal: Intact, even-toned for the person, no spreading redness, non-healing sores, or changing moles; warm and well-perfused.
common_problems: Eczema, psoriasis, cellulitis, abscess, shingles, impetigo, hives, fungal infections, skin cancer/melanoma, pressure sores.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Lymph nodes, spleen & defence
systems.overview: The lymphatic system drains fluid from tissues, filters it through lymph nodes, and is central to the immune defence against infection.

structures.name: Lymph nodes
structures.detail: Small filters clustered in the neck, armpits, groin, chest, and abdomen — swell when fighting infection.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.detail: LUQ organ that filters blood and supports immunity (can be injured/enlarged).

structures.name: Thymus & marrow
structures.detail: Make and train immune cells.

structures.name: Tonsils/adenoids
structures.detail: Immune tissue guarding the throat.

systems.normal: Nodes usually not felt, or small, soft, mobile, and briefly tender with a nearby infection; no drenching night sweats or unexplained weight loss.
common_problems: Reactive swollen glands (infection), glandular fever, lymphoma, leukaemia, enlarged/ruptured spleen, immune deficiency.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Eyes, ears, nose & tongue
systems.overview: The special senses gather information about the world: sight, hearing and balance, smell, and taste.

structures.name: Eye
structures.detail: Cornea and lens focus light onto the retina; the iris sets pupil size; the optic nerve carries images to the brain.

structures.name: Ear
structures.detail: Outer ear → eardrum → middle-ear bones → cochlea (hearing) and semicircular canals (balance).

structures.name: Nose
structures.detail: Smell receptors high in the nose; also warms and filters air.

structures.name: Tongue
structures.detail: Taste buds (sweet, salt, sour, bitter, umami) and helps speech and swallowing.

systems.normal: Clear vision, equal reactive pupils, normal hearing and balance, normal smell and taste.
common_problems: Conjunctivitis, glaucoma, retinal detachment, ear infections, hearing loss, vertigo (inner ear), sinus problems, loss of smell/taste.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Female reproductive anatomy
systems.overview: The adult female reproductive system produces eggs and sex hormones, supports menstruation, and carries a pregnancy. (Educational/clinical reference.)

structures.name: Ovaries
structures.detail: Two glands that release an egg each cycle and make oestrogen and progesterone.

structures.name: Fallopian tubes
structures.detail: Carry the egg toward the uterus; usual site of fertilisation (and of ectopic pregnancy if it implants there).

structures.name: Uterus (womb)
structures.detail: Muscular organ whose lining builds up and sheds each month, and where a pregnancy grows; the cervix is its neck.

structures.name: Vagina & vulva
structures.detail: The vagina connects the cervix to the outside; the vulva is the external genital area.

structures.name: Menstrual cycle
structures.detail: ~21–35 days: lining thickens, an egg is released (ovulation ~mid-cycle), then the lining sheds (period) if no pregnancy.

structures.name: Breasts
structures.detail: Glandular tissue for milk, plus ducts and fat.

systems.normal: Regular-for-the-person cycles, no bleeding between periods/after sex/after menopause, no new breast lump or nipple change, no severe pelvic pain.
common_problems: Period problems, endometriosis, PCOS, fibroids, ovarian cysts, PID, ectopic pregnancy, menopause symptoms, cervical/uterine/ovarian/breast cancer.
Bleeding after menopause, or a new breast lump, should always be checked.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)

systems.title: Male reproductive anatomy
systems.overview: The adult male reproductive system makes sperm and sex hormones and delivers them. It overlaps with the urinary tract (shared urethra). (Educational/clinical reference.)

structures.name: Testes
structures.detail: Two glands in the scrotum that make sperm and testosterone; kept cooler than body temperature.

structures.name: Epididymis & vas deferens
structures.detail: Store and carry sperm.

structures.name: Prostate
structures.detail: Gland below the bladder surrounding the urethra; adds fluid to semen and can enlarge with age and affect urine flow.

structures.name: Penis & urethra
structures.detail: The urethra carries both urine and semen; erectile tissue fills with blood for an erection.

structures.name: Seminal vesicles
structures.detail: Add most of the fluid in semen.

systems.normal: Comfortable, symmetrical testes with no new lump; a normal urine stream; no pain, discharge, or blood in urine/semen.
common_problems: Testicular torsion (sudden severe pain — emergency) or lump (needs checking), epididymitis, prostatitis, enlarged prostate (BPH), erectile problems, STIs, testicular/prostate cancer.
systems.source: HIVE Doctor original anatomy reference (standard public-domain anatomy, re-expressed)
